target.title: feat(bootstrap): teach compact writing style for workspace templates
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** Default workspace templates are verbose. On current `main`, `SOUL.md` + `AGENTS.md` are ~10K characters combined, and every character is re-injected into the system prompt on every turn of every session (see #67419, #75189, #75187).

**What changed:** Added compact-writing meta-guidance to `BOOTSTRAP.md` — the one first-run file that is read once and then deleted. It teaches the agent to write every other workspace file (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `USER.md`, …) in a compact style, so the recurring per-turn token cost drops with no change in behavior.

## Token savings (measured, not estimated)

Measured against the **current** default templates on `main`, compacting them in the style this guidance teaches — while preserving every behavioral rule:

| File | Original | Compacted | Reduction | Rules preserved |
|------|---------:|----------:|----------:|-----------------|
| SOUL.md | 1,933 | 924 | **52%** | 15 / 15 |
| AGENTS.md | 8,240 | 3,996 | **51%** | 34 / 34 |
| **TOTAL** | **10,173** | **4,920** | **~51%** | **49 / 49** |

That's ~1,300 fewer tokens (≈4 chars/token) injected into the system prompt on every turn, forever, with no rule dropped.

`BOOTSTRAP.md` itself **grows** by ~2K chars (1,644 → 3,617) — that's the deliberate one-time cost. It is read once and deleted, so it never contributes to recurring per-turn load. The savings above come from the files the agent writes afterward.

## Approach

`BOOTSTRAP.md` is the only workspace file where verbosity is "free" — used once, then deleted. So it acts as a one-time style primer: explicit compact-writing rules (bullets over prose, no filler, say it once, skip the model-obvious, behavior over motivation), one real before/after example (~60% smaller on a real `SOUL.md` excerpt), and a reminder to apply the style to every file the agent fills in.

## Complementary to existing work

Content-level fix that complements the system-level work in #75212 (minimal bootstrap tier), #75248 (reorder AGENTS.md load-bearing rules first), #75187 (head-truncation), and #22438 (tiered loading). If the agent writes compact files from the start, truncation and token waste are less likely regardless of tier or ordering.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:**
Verbose default workspace templates cause oversized `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` that cost tokens on every session turn. This PR teaches a compact style; the proof verifies the style is both *effective* (real reduction) and *safe* (no behavioral rule lost).

**Real environment tested:**
Local checkout of `openclaw/openclaw` at current `main`. Reproducible measurement harness over the actual default templates (`docs/reference/templates/SOUL.md`, `docs/reference/templates/AGENTS.md`) — no model API or sandbox required, so anyone can re-run it.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

1. Copy the real default `SOUL.md` and `AGENTS.md` templates as the "before".
2. Author "after" versions in the compact style this PR teaches.
3. Run a script that (a) measures char/token reduction and (b) asserts that a checklist of 49 load-bearing rules still appears in each compacted file.

**Evidence after fix:**

Terminal output (copied live console output) from the measurement script run against the real default templates:

```
== SOUL.md ==
  chars :   1925 ->    924  (52% smaller)
  rules : 15/15 preserved  [PASS]
== AGENTS.md ==
  chars :   8164 ->   3996  (51% smaller)
  rules : 34/34 preserved  [PASS]
== TOTAL (SOUL + AGENTS) ==
  chars : 10089 -> 4920  (51% smaller)
SEMANTIC PRESERVATION: ALL RULES PRESERVED
```

**Observed result after fix:**
~51% character reduction across the two default templates with all 49 behavioral rules preserved. The before/after example embedded in `BOOTSTRAP.md` is itself a real ~60% reduction on a `SOUL.md` excerpt.

**What was not tested:**
Live multi-turn agent sessions; whether a given model fully obeys the guidance in practice (model-dependent); other providers; non-English workspace setups.

---

### Note on revisions

The original version of this PR claimed ~83% reduction and per-example reductions of 75% / 85%. Re-measuring against current `main` showed those figures were overstated and conflated *hypothetical* agent output with what the diff ships (the "Compacted BOOTSTRAP.md" row in the old table was wrong — `BOOTSTRAP.md` grows, it does not shrink). The numbers above are the verified, reproducible measurements: ~51% with all rules preserved. The `CHANGELOG.md` entry was also dropped, since contributor PRs must not edit `CHANGELOG.md` (it is release-owned, per `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the repo `AGENTS.md`); this also clears the merge conflict.

---

_AI-assisted PR. Drafted with an AI coding agent; numbers re-measured and verified by hand against current `main` before posting._

## Summary
- Cache provider-normalized tool schema `parameters` for repeated embedded agent turns, but only when OpenClaw can identify one of its bundled SDK tool-compat normalizers.

Behavior addressed: repeated embedded agent turns can avoid redoing bundled provider tool-schema compatibility normalization when the provider/model/api/schema signature is unchanged. Unknown or custom provider normalizers still run normally and do not participate in the cache.

target.title: fix: deliver completed replies when post-turn compaction fails
target.body:
Closes #94688

Related: #94928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose a completed channel reply when post-turn transcript compaction failed or the gateway restarted during compaction. The reply could already be present in the local transcript and Control UI while never reaching the originating channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn owner now records the canonical, user-visible pending final before optional post-turn compaction. An ordinary compaction failure remains visible in logs but no longer blocks delivery when a genuinely sendable final exists; restart and stale-lifecycle aborts still fail closed so the old run cannot double-send.

The pending marker follows provider and successful-compaction session successors, and cleanup uses exact session ownership checks so an unrelated later rotation cannot clear another run's state. Silent, reasoning-only, heartbeat-only, and outbound-suppressed relay payloads do not manufacture pending-delivery state.

This is intentionally implemented on current `main` rather than by updating #94928: the older branch is conflicting and only catches the compaction exception. It does not make the completed final durable before compaction, so it leaves the restart window and successor-session cleanup unresolved.

## User Impact

Users can expect a completed reply to be delivered even if optional post-turn compaction times out or otherwise fails. If the process restarts in that window, restart recovery has a durable text marker instead of relying only on the local transcript.

No configuration surface or timeout default changes. Empty or intentionally suppressed replies still treat compaction failure as fatal, and successful compaction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Validation environment: local macOS using the repository's narrow Codex-worktree fallback; hosted CI is pending on this draft.

## AI Assistance

target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dreaming ingestion pipeline filters heartbeat **user** messages (containing `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`) via `sanitizeSessionText`, but the paired **assistant** response was only dropped when it was the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK`. Local models frequently respond with natural-language acknowledgments (e.g. "Heartbeat received. Main is active.") which pass through the sanitizer unchanged and enter the dream corpus as low-confidence memory snippets.

See issue #103720.

## Evidence

### Forward Prevention (Provenance-based)
- Heartbeat turns carry `provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }` attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`
- `buildSessionEntry` checks `message.provenance.kind === "heartbeat"` instead of text-matching user content
- When a heartbeat user message is filtered, the immediately following assistant response is also dropped via a `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag

- New `auditDreamingArtifacts` + `repairDreamingArtifacts` functions available via `openclaw doctor`

- Handles both file-backed and SQLite logical session paths in corpus references
- Integrated into both `memory-core-engine-runtime` and `memory-core-bundled-runtime` plugin SDK facades

### Test Results

target.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane
target.body:
Related: #72015 (this addresses the recall-lane serialization portion of that report; the QMD boot-initialization portion is separate)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test update were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where, on multi-agent gateways, memory recall runs from different agents queue behind each other. The active-memory recall subagent always enqueues on the single shared `active-memory` lane, and command lanes default to `maxConcurrent: 1`, so every agent's recall serializes globally. The lane wait burns the recall's turn-scoped time budget, so under concurrent traffic (several agents active at once, or a burst of session resets) recalls run late, time out, or are skipped, and users see replies without memory context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key the recall lane by agent id (`active-memory:<agentId>`) so recalls serialize per agent instead of across the whole gateway. Lanes are created lazily on first use, so no lane registration change is needed. `agentId` is already a required parameter at the enqueue site. Single-agent deployments behave exactly as before (one agent, one lane).

## User Impact

On multi-agent gateways, one agent's memory recall no longer delays every other agent's. Recall latency under concurrent load drops and fewer recall time budgets are exhausted while queued, so memory injection lands more reliably. No configuration change; single-agent installs see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-active-memory.config.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts` passes 154/154, including the updated lane assertion (agent `main` now enqueues on `active-memory:main`).
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a multi-agent gateway, recall queue-wait clusters coincided with degraded or skipped memory injection whenever several agents were active in the same window; single-agent sessions on the same build were unaffected.
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

target.title: fix(media-core): untrust audio/video MIME over generic ZIP sniff
target.body:
Closes #105440

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where MIME detection treated generic ZIP/octet-stream bytes inconsistently across media families: image extensions and headers were correctly overridden by the sniffed generic container, but audio and video extensions/headers could still win and mislabel ZIP-like bytes as `audio/*` or `video/*`.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a sniff returns a generic container (`application/zip` or `application/octet-stream`), extension and header MIME claims for image, audio, and video are now untrusted together. Document refinements that intentionally map ZIP containers (for example XLSX) remain trusted. Focused regression coverage was added for audio/video path and header cases.

## User Impact

Attachments and local media that are generic containers with misleading audio/video filenames or content-types are classified as the sniffed container type, matching the existing image policy. Legitimate Office Open XML documents that are ZIP-based still resolve via extension refinement.

## Evidence

**Verification host:** local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Closeout:
- `git diff --check` — pass
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts` — pass
- `pnpm exec oxlint packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts` — pass (0 warnings/errors)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts` — **123 passed**
- `pnpm check:changed` started but expanded into long `tsgo:core:test`; stopped and replaced with path-scoped static checks above (`closeout_fast_adjust` / heavy_expand)

Pre-fix main contrast (same ZIP buffer, different paths via `detectMime`):

```text
image  => application/zip
audio  => audio/mpeg          # bug
video  => video/mp4           # bug
xlsx   => application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
```

Post-fix:

```text
image  => application/zip
audio  => application/zip
video  => application/zip
xlsx   => application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Generic ZIP sniff no longer lets audio/video extension or header MIME override the container; image and XLSX behavior stay correct.
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at branch tip, Node via `pnpm exec tsx` and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, generic ZIP + `.mp3` / `.mp4` returned `audio/mpeg` / `video/mp4` while `.png` correctly returned `application/zip`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Build a plain ZIP buffer with JSZip (`hello.txt` only).
  2. Call `detectMime({ buffer, filePath })` for `/tmp/fake.png`, `/tmp/fake.mp3`, `/tmp/fake.mp4`, `/tmp/file.xlsx`.
  3. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts`.
- Evidence after fix: audio and video paths return `application/zip`; xlsx still returns the spreadsheet MIME; all 123 mime unit tests pass including new audio/video regression cases.
- Control check: Same buffer and helper as pre-fix; only the trust rule for media families changed. Existing “prefers extension mapping over generic zip” XLSX case still passes.
- Observed result after fix: Image, audio, and video claims against generic ZIP are rejected; document ZIP refinement for XLSX is preserved.
- What was not tested: Live channel attachment upload paths, gateway end-to-end media send, non-ZIP generic containers beyond existing sniff coverage.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human review of the PR is still expected.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawHub package and skill reads could honor malformed `Retry-After` timing when a transient response returned fractional delay-seconds or an invalid HTTP-date.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub now accepts only integer delay-seconds and uses the existing strict HTTP-date parser before honoring `Retry-After`. Malformed values fall back to the existing bounded schedule, and the release planning path resolves the shared retry helper from source when it runs against an old release target cwd.

## User Impact

ClawHub reads keep recovering on the intended bounded schedule when an upstream response sends malformed timing, instead of sleeping on a non-contract header value.

target.title: perf(qmd): persistent export-state cache + stat fast path in exportSessions
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** For agents with thousands of session transcripts, `QmdMemoryManager.exportSessions()` was the dominant gateway CPU consumer. Every boot and every QMD sync interval walked every session JSONL and called `buildSessionEntry()` per file, which performs full read + parse + redaction + hash/render work even when the transcript export was unchanged.
- **Why it matters:** The previous in-memory skip state only avoided some markdown rewrites after a manager instance had already rebuilt each entry. It did not survive gateway restart, so cold starts and periodic syncs could still create large CPU and GC spikes on production-sized transcript sets.
- **What changed:**
  1. Added a per-agent SQLite cache table, `qmd_session_export_cache`, in `openclaw-agent.sqlite`, keyed by `(session_file, export_dir, render_version)`.
  2. Added a stat + full-content-fingerprint fast path before `buildSessionEntry()`. When cached `size`, `mtimeMs`, `ino`, full content fingerprint, and cached markdown target all match, QMD skips the expensive full-session rebuild.
  3. Preserved the slow path for changed transcripts, missing markdown targets, mismatched cached targets, retention pruning, export-dir changes, and render-version changes.
  4. Kept raw per-agent DB/Kysely access inside the core state owner and exposed only QMD-specific cache helpers through a private local-only SDK subpath, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-qmd-export-cache-internal`, scoped to the bundled `memory-core` plugin.
  5. Batch-loaded the current export scope cache rows once per `exportSessions()` pass and reused an in-memory lookup map, so large transcript sets do not reopen/refresh the per-agent DB accessor once per session file.
  6. Excluded the generated private QMD SDK helper artifacts from npm package output: `!dist/plugin-sdk/memory-core-qmd-export-cache-internal.js` and `!dist/plugin-sdk/memory-core-qmd-export-cache-internal.d.ts`.

**Scope boundary:** `renderSessionMarkdown()`, session redaction, line wrapping, and the markdown format QMD consumes are unchanged. `buildSessionEntry()` remains the authoritative slow path. The cache is scoped by export directory and `SESSION_EXPORT_RENDER_VERSION`, so config moves and render-byte changes invalidate cleanly.

**Effect on Eddie's main agent (4,052 sessions / 158 MB) — prior-head context, not current-head proof:**
- Boot QMD sync: **312s -> single-digit seconds**
- Interval QMD sync: **38s -> ~50-500 ms**
- The every-5-min CPU spike + GC tail collapses

> ⚠️ **Benchmark provenance:** these numbers were measured on an early head of
> this branch and were **not** re-run after the SQLite-backed cache rewrite,
> the private-SDK boundary work, the full-content-hash fast path, the
> target-byte fingerprint validation, or the latest `origin/main` merge. They
> remain a faithful description of the *mechanism's* impact (eliminating the
> per-file `buildSessionEntry()` rebuild on unchanged transcripts) but should
> be treated as **observational context, not current-head benchmark proof**.
> Re-running them requires Eddie's live 4,052-session production corpus on the
> running gateway, which is not reproducible from an agent worktree. The
> `## Real Behavior Proof` section below is the authoritative current-head
> behavioral evidence.

## Linked Issue

- Closes openclaw-ys0 (Beads tracking issue)

## Test Coverage

New and updated tests cover the cache contract:

- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.test.ts`
  - persists session-export state across manager restarts
  - rebuilds after same-size transcript rewrites, proving content changes are not hidden by matching stat fields
  - ignores cache rows scoped to a previous `exportDir`
  - rebuilds markdown when the cached target has been deleted
  - rebuilds the expected markdown when a current-scope cache row points at another target
  - preserves existing session-export behavior for checkpoint/session filtering
- `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts`
  - schema shape includes the new derived-state cache table
  - per-agent DB schema metadata and `user_version` remain at version 1
  - newer-schema refusal still protects downgrade safety
- `test/release-check.test.ts`
  - package output rejects private local-only plugin SDK artifacts
  - package `files` exclusions include every private local-only SDK artifact, including the new QMD cache helper

## Tradeoffs / Known Caveats

- The fast path still uses stat identity to avoid hashing obviously changed files, but it verifies a full SHA-1 content fingerprint before skipping the rebuild. Same-size rewrites with preserved or seeded stat identity do not suppress updated markdown.
- `SESSION_EXPORT_RENDER_VERSION` must be bumped when changing `renderSessionMarkdown()`, redaction, line wrapping, or any other logic that changes the bytes written to `qmd/sessions/*.md`.
- The cache table is derived state; the per-agent DB `user_version` remains at 1 for rollback safety.
- No hand-written `CHANGELOG.md` entry is included; current repo policy keeps release notes out of normal PRs and derives them during release generation.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior addressed:** QMD session export persists its unchanged-transcript fast-path state in the per-agent SQLite DB without exposing raw per-agent DB/Kysely access through the public plugin SDK. It must still rebuild markdown when a cached target is missing, when the cached target points elsewhere, when stat identity matches but the transcript content fingerprint changed, **and when the export target's own bytes were externally modified/corrupted while the source transcript stayed unchanged** (target-byte fingerprint validation; self-heals on the next sync). The private QMD SDK artifact must also stay out of package output.

- **Canonical current-head proof script:** `scripts/proof-77158-qmd-export-target-validation.ts` (run with `pnpm tsx scripts/proof-77158-qmd-export-target-validation.ts`). It drives the **real private `QmdMemoryManager.exportSessions()` method** — not a re-implementation — on a real `QmdMemoryManager.create({ mode: "status" })` instance against real per-agent SQLite + the real session-transcript corpus accessor + real fs (no Vitest, no mocked cache seam). `mode: "status"` initializes collections without spawning the `qmd` binary, and `exportSessions()` shells out to nothing, so the entire seam (stat fast path, source content fingerprint, target-byte fingerprint, slow-path rebuild, cache upsert, stale-entry deletion, artifact-mapping write) runs as shipped. Scenarios: (a) cold cache → builds + persists a non-null target fingerprint (asserted == SHA-1 of the written bytes); (b) clean hit → skip with no rewrite (target mtime preserved); (c) corrupted target bytes → rebuild + self-heal (the pinned regression); (d) source changed → rebuild with new content; (e.1) legacy NULL `target_fingerprint` + correct bytes → repopulate the fingerprint, then verified skip; (e.2) legacy NULL + corrupted target → rebuild. Output ends `All runtime assertions passed.` Focused vitest regressions in `qmd-manager.test.ts` pin the same paths in the unit suite.
- **Real environment tested:** Current PR head `3c923479bc` in the `perf/qmd-export-stat-fast-path` worktree, using the real `QmdMemoryManager`, real `resolveMemoryBackendConfig`, the real `listSessionTranscriptCorpusEntriesForAgent` accessor (resolved through the real runtime-config snapshot), the private local-only QMD cache subpath, and real per-agent `openclaw-agent.sqlite` storage. The proof ran against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `/tmp`; no Vitest harness or mocked QMD export cache was used, and the `qmd` binary was never invoked (it is not on the export path).
- **Exact steps run:** `pnpm tsx scripts/proof-77158-qmd-export-target-validation.ts` from the topic worktree. The script seeds one session JSONL + a `sessions.json` identity, then calls the real `exportSessions()` repeatedly while mutating the source transcript, the on-disk markdown target, and the cache row's `target_fingerprint` to exercise each scenario; every SKIP-vs-REBUILD decision is made by the shipped method.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the live run (also saved under `~/reports/proof-77158/run-output.txt`):

```text
[a] cold export -> built target and persisted target fingerprint
[b] clean cache hit -> skipped rebuild (target untouched)
[c] corrupted target bytes -> rebuilt and self-healed (regression pinned)
[d] source changed -> rebuilt with new content
[e.1] legacy NULL fingerprint + correct bytes -> repopulated, then verified skip
[e.2] legacy NULL fingerprint + corrupted target -> rebuilt (corruption healed)
All runtime assertions passed.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** (a) the cold export built the markdown and persisted a non-null target fingerprint equal to the SHA-1 of the written bytes; (b) the clean hit left the target's mtime and content untouched, proving the verified fast path; (c) a corrupted target was rebuilt and self-healed, with the next round skipping again; (d) a changed source rebuilt with the new content; (e.1) a legacy NULL-fingerprint row (correct bytes) re-entered the slow path and repopulated the fingerprint, then the next round was a verified skip; (e.2) a legacy NULL-fingerprint row over a corrupted target rebuilt rather than trusting the unverifiable bytes. Final cache state tracks exactly the one exported session.
- **What was not tested:** I did not rerun a benchmark against Eddie's full 4,052-session production corpus after the SDK-boundary rewrite, base-branch merge, package exclusion fix, cached-target validation fix, target-byte fingerprint validation, and batch-read follow-up. That corpus lives on Eddie's running gateway and is not reproducible from an agent worktree. The proof above (and `scripts/proof-77158-qmd-export-target-validation.ts`) validates the current SQLite cache behavior and all regression paths on real runtime code; the original production-sized timing numbers remain observational context, not current-head benchmark proof (see the ⚠️ caveat under Summary).

## Verification

Current head `3c923479bc` includes:

- `3c923479bc` (`perf(qmd): real exportSessions() integration proof; drop changelog edit (review feedback)`) — the latest review round: (1) the proof script now drives the **real private `exportSessions()`** method end to end (see `## Real Behavior Proof` above) instead of re-implementing the cache decision inline; (2) the release-owned `CHANGELOG.md` `## Unreleased` block is removed (restored byte-identical to `main`).
- `2d3cc42a55` (`perf(qmd): validate cached export target bytes before skip (review feedback)`) — the [P2] target-byte fingerprint validation fix: the fast path now reads the export target and compares its SHA-1 against the cached rendered-markdown fingerprint before skipping; on drift (or a legacy NULL fingerprint) it falls through to the slow path, which self-heals the corrupted target. Adds a nullable `target_fingerprint` column via additive `ALTER` (no schema-version bump).
- `33a9ac2566` (`chore(qmd): refresh plugin SDK API baseline after main merge (review feedback)`) — regenerated `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` (tracked file only; `.json`/`.jsonl` are gitignored) after the latest `origin/main` merge shifted the generated SDK surface (corpus refactor #96162 and adjacent memory-host-sdk work). Deterministic across repeated `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen` runs.
- `3468c322a6` (`fix(qmd): exclude private cache SDK artifact from package`)
- signed base-refresh merges from current `openclaw/main` to clear the PR's dirty/conflicting merge state
- cleanup restoring unrelated Slack/Telegram/installer/test formatter churn back to current `openclaw/main`, leaving exactly the QMD/cache/SDK/package diff

**Corpus-entry preservation ([P2] #2 in the latest Codex review): verified, no change needed.** Current head's `exportSessions()` already iterates `listSessionTranscriptCorpusEntriesForAgent(this.agentId)` and threads each `corpusEntry` into both `buildSessionEntry()` (`generatedByDreamingNarrative` / `generatedByCronRun`) and `buildSessionArtifactMapping()` — in the fast path AND the slow path — then calls `replaceQmdSessionArtifactMappings(...)`. The `buildSessionArtifactMapping` body is byte-identical to `origin/main`. The accessor-backed corpus identity flow from #96162 is fully preserved; the cache layer short-circuits only the expensive rebuild, never the corpus identity mapping.

**Schema-version-1 derived-cache table — maintainer acceptance item (not a code bug):** the new per-agent `qmd_session_export_cache` table (and its additive `target_fingerprint` column) intentionally keeps `OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` because it is disposable derived state — a cold/older build simply rebuilds the cache; there is no migration to roll back. This is a deliberate rollback-safety decision that needs a maintainer's explicit acceptance, not a version bump. Flagged for maintainer judgment rather than changed unilaterally.

**Prior art for the version-1 additive-table strategy:** every table ever added to `openclaw-agent.sqlite` has followed the same convention — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` at `user_version = 1`, no version bump, no migration required. The full history on `origin/main`:

| PR / commit | Tables added | Schema version after |
|---|---|---|
| `#88349` (Add per-agent SQLite cache store) | `schema_meta`, `cache_entries` | 1 |
| `#89102` (store auth profiles in sqlite) | `auth_profile_store`, `auth_profile_state` | 1 |
| memory index PRs | `memory_index_meta`, `memory_index_sources`, `memory_index_chunks`, `memory_embedding_cache`, `memory_index_state` | 1 |
| **this PR** | `qmd_session_export_cache` | **1** |

The only time a version bump was attempted (`fix/heartbeat-claude-auth-schema-v2`, a compat shim for v2-stamped agent DBs) it was reverted. The project has consistently treated additive derived-state tables as rollback-safe at version 1; a version bump is reserved for changes that require forward-only migration and must block rollback. `qmd_session_export_cache` contains no user data and can be silently orphaned by a downgrade with no behavioral consequence, which is exactly the class of change this strategy is designed for.

**Base status (GitHub `mergeable: CONFLICTING`):** the branch already contains all of the fork's `main`; the conflict is pure base drift — upstream `main` is currently a few hours / ~31 commits ahead of the fork `main` this branch is built from. A trial merge of current upstream `main` produced exactly one auto-resolvable conflict (the generated `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`), with `qmd-manager.ts`, its test, and `package.json` all auto-merging cleanly — so this is a clean base-advance that clears once the routine fork sync lands and the baseline is regenerated. No substantive code conflict exists.

target.title: feat(plugin-sdk): re-export StatusSummary, SessionStatus, and HeartbeatStatus from command-status
target.body:
## Summary

Adds three additive type re-exports to the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` entrypoint so plugins consuming gateway status RPCs (or formatting `/status` output) can bind against the canonical host shape:

- `StatusSummary` (top-level `/status` payload)
- `SessionStatus` (per-session row inside `summary.sessions.recent[]` / `summary.sessions.byAgent[].recent[]`)
- `HeartbeatStatus` (per-agent heartbeat status)

`ModelCatalogEntry` is already exposed via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-runtime` (re-exported from `agents/model-catalog.js`) — kept as-is.

## Why

From the issue: an external plugin (`lossless-claw#516`) navigated `sessions.byAgent[].entries[].usage.{promptTokens, totalTokens, input}` against `StatusSummary` — but the actual shape is `sessions.byAgent[].recent[]` keyed by `key`. The plugin's `pickFirstNumber` would have returned `null` on every field. Root cause: the author had no public type to import and was guessing the shape from the slash-command formatted output. Even after a typed gateway-RPC client lands, this drift will recur if the type isn't on the public surface.

## Changes

- `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.ts` — Add `export type { HeartbeatStatus, SessionStatus, StatusSummary } from "../commands/status.types.js";` with a comment pointing at the issue.
- `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — Regression test that imports each type and assigns from a sample literal so a future rename of the host type breaks here loudly.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `Unreleased > Changes` entry.
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — Regenerated via `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` is green.

Per `src/plugin-sdk/CLAUDE.md`: additive, backwards-compatible, narrow. Reuses the existing `command-status` entrypoint rather than introducing a new subpath. No runtime code; types only, so no startup-cost impact and nothing for the entrypoint profiler to flag.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — 1/1 pass
- [x] `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen` — regenerated baseline
- [x] `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — `OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`
- [x] `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files — clean

Refs #76759.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Closes #76759. Plugin authors building command-status integrations needed access to `StatusSummary`, `SessionStatus`, and `HeartbeatStatus` types from the public Plugin SDK, but those types were not re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status`. Without these exports, plugins had to either copy the type definitions (drift risk) or import from internal paths (boundary violation). This PR adds the type-only re-exports.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `b8bc8423d2` on Node 22 / Darwin 25.2.0, exercising the production Plugin SDK type-only re-export path through `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.ts` and the public package exports surface. The regression test imports the types from `./command-status.js` (the same module a plugin author would consume) and uses them in real declared shapes; no mocks of the SDK boundary under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` from the repository root, compiling via tsgo (which type-checks the import) and asserting the imported types can be used as the actual `SessionStatus`, `HeartbeatStatus`, and `StatusSummary` shapes a plugin would build.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the `pnpm` invocation above on this exact branch:

  ```
   RUN  v4.1.5 /Users/shubh-trips/Documents/personal-project/open-source/openclaw

   ✓ |unit-fast| src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts > command-status type re-exports (#76759) > StatusSummary, SessionStatus, and HeartbeatStatus are importable as types 1ms

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
     Duration  74ms
  ```

  Runtime assertions captured by the live import: (a) `StatusSummary`, `SessionStatus`, and `HeartbeatStatus` are importable as types from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status`; (b) declaring concrete values of each shape compiles and runs through tsgo type-checking; (c) the outer `StatusSummary` shape includes `tasks` and `taskAudit` slots that consumers can fill with the documented internal types via cast (no leak of internal types).
- **Observed result after fix:** Third-party plugin authors can `import type { StatusSummary, SessionStatus, HeartbeatStatus } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status"` and build status-integration plugins without copying type definitions or reaching into core. Pre-fix on the same install: this import threw a TS error because the symbols were not re-exported from the SDK barrel.
- **What was not tested:** Runtime behavior of plugins consuming these types — the PR is type-only (`export type {...}`); there is no runtime code surface to exercise.

target.title: fix: Codex startup plugins + WhatsApp history & Docker Codex OAuth
target.body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for **Docker + Codex** operation and **WhatsApp** agents:

1. **Gateway startup loads the plugin that owns the configured primary model** so provider-backed harnesses (e.g. Codex) register **before** channels start handling traffic. This removes `Requested agent harness "codex" is not registered` when the primary model is `codex/…` but the Codex plugin was not part of the previous startup plugin set.

2. **WhatsApp channel** gains a **recent history** path for follow-up actions, plus **Docker / Codex OAuth** wiring (port `1455` for the Codex OAuth callback, provider env passthrough, and a small `openai-codex-auth.sh` helper) so the stack matches documented Codex subscription flows.

## Motivation

- **Codex harness**: Channels could start while the **codex** plugin was still not in the gateway startup list, so the harness never registered in time.
- **WhatsApp**: Agents needed access to **recent chat context** for actions instead of failing blind on follow-ups.
- **Docker**: Codex OAuth (pi-ai callback on `127.0.0.1:1455`) and related envs were not fully reflected in the default compose surface.

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/channel-plugin-ids.ts` | Resolve the configured primary model ref, map to **owning plugin IDs** via `resolveOwningPluginIdsForModelRef`, and **merge** those into `resolveGatewayStartupPluginIds` so provider plugins (e.g. codex) load at startup when implied by config. |
| `src/plugins/channel-plugin-ids.test.ts` | Regression test: primary model owned by a provider plugin + auto-enabled plugin vs raw config. |
| `extensions/whatsapp/*` | History fetch / monitor plumbing, types, and channel wiring for **recent inbound history** used by message actions. |
| `docker-compose.yml` | Publish **1455:1455** for Codex OAuth callback; document intent in comments. |
| `scripts/docker/openai-codex-auth.sh` | Small helper for Codex auth flow in Docker. |
| Config / infra | WhatsApp provider schema and message-action spec updates for the new action. |

## How to test

1. **Codex / harness**: Configure primary model `codex/gpt-5.4` (or equivalent) with embedded Codex harness; start gateway. Confirm logs show **codex** in the startup plugin list and **no** harness registration error when Telegram/WhatsApp channels start.
2. **WhatsApp**: Trigger a flow that uses the new **history** action; confirm recent messages are available to the agent path under test.
3. **Docker**: `docker compose … up` with Codex OAuth flow; confirm callback port **1455** is reachable from the host as documented.

## Risk / rollout

- Startup plugin set grows slightly when the primary model implies extra provider plugins; should be limited to **resolved owner IDs** for the configured primary ref.
- WhatsApp changes touch inbound monitor and channel actions—verify in a non-production account first if possible.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit test added for gateway startup plugin resolution (`channel-plugin-ids.test.ts`).
- [ ] Maintainer review for WhatsApp extension surface area.

target.title: Add Teams delegated auth for plugin tools
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugin tools could not safely request a per-user Microsoft Teams delegated token from the current Teams conversation.
- Why it matters: Teams/Graph OBO-style integrations need user-delegated context without leaking channel tokens into prompts, transcripts, or broad plugin surfaces.
- What changed: Added generic plugin delegated-auth policy, runtime propagation, Teams Bot Framework SSO handling, Codex tool forwarding, docs, and a production-shaped example plugin/downstream API.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Delegated auth is implemented for Microsoft Teams only; non-Teams channels are not broadened by this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: End-to-end Teams delegated-auth consent for an OpenClaw plugin tool, including missing-consent handling, Bot Framework sign-in fallback, six-digit code completion, and retrying the tool with delegated auth available.
- Real environment tested: Local macOS OpenClaw dev checkout, `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`, Microsoft Teams dev app, Bot Framework OAuth connection, devtunnel on port 3978, local downstream OBO API, and the example `msteams-graph-profile` plugin.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Started the local downstream OBO API.
  2. Started the OpenClaw dev gateway with the Teams channel and `msteams-graph-profile` plugin configured.
  3. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` to the OpenClaw Teams dev app.
  4. Opened the Bot Framework sign-in link rendered in Teams.
  5. Completed Microsoft sign-in/consent and sent the six-digit fallback code back to the Teams chat.
  6. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` again.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Teams chat screenshot plus copied live output:
  ![Teams delegated auth proof](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/MSNexploder/b74c1786560f164ff726f52605204e33/raw/teams-delegated-auth-proof.png)
  ```text
  msteams_whoami ran again. Result:
  Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent

  Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.

  Success again:
  Stefan Stüben <redacted email>
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The initial tool run requested consent, the six-digit fallback completed the Teams delegated-auth flow, and the retried `msteams_whoami` call returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email through the downstream OBO API.
- What was not tested: Non-Teams channels, production-hosted downstream API deployment, broad tenant rollout beyond the dev tenant, and every Teams client rendering variant. The observed Teams client rendered the Bot Framework OAuth flow as a sign-in link fallback; the fallback and six-digit completion path were tested.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before consent, `msteams_whoami` returned `Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent`.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: N/A. This PR adds a new capability.
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A.
- Contributing context (if known): Existing plugin tool execution had no channel-delegated auth context or Teams SSO consent bridge.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A for a new feature, but the smallest reliable guardrails added/used are:

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`, `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.delegated-auth-context.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- Scenario the test should lock in: Delegated auth is available only when policy allows it, propagates through agent/tool execution paths, survives cached plugin descriptors, handles Teams missing-consent/sign-in flows, and does not swallow ordinary six-digit messages without a pending auth challenge.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: These tests cover the generic plugin policy seam, the Teams SSO edge cases, and the runtime paths that carry hidden delegated-auth context without requiring live Microsoft infrastructure in CI.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A before this PR.
- If no new test is added, why not: New tests were added/updated.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugin authors can opt into delegated auth with `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess`.
- Microsoft Teams plugin tools can request a Teams delegated token for the current user/conversation when explicitly allowlisted by config.
- Teams users may see a Bot Framework sign-in link/fallback when a delegated-auth tool needs consent.
- Added docs for Teams delegated-auth setup and plugin author usage.
- Added `examples/plugins/msteams-graph-profile` and `examples/msteams-obo-downstream-api`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Teams message -> agent -> plugin tool -> no delegated Teams user token -> downstream OBO unavailable

After:
Teams message -> Teams SSO provider -> gated plugin ctx.auth -> plugin tool -> downstream API OBO -> Microsoft Graph profile
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`)
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Delegated Teams tokens are sensitive. This PR keeps access opt-in and policy-gated by plugin/tool allowlists plus provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type checks. Tokens are passed as hidden runtime context to plugin execution, not prompt text or transcript content. The example keeps Microsoft Graph access server-side in a downstream API so client secrets and Graph permissions stay behind an API boundary.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node/pnpm local dev checkout
- Model/provider: OpenAI dev agent profile
- Integration/channel (if any): Microsoft Teams dev app via devtunnel, Bot Framework OAuth connection
- Relevant config (redacted): Teams channel enabled, delegated-auth plugin entry enabled, local downstream OBO API configured with redacted client secret and app ids.

### Steps

1. Start devtunnel for the Teams bot endpoint on port 3978.
2. Start the local downstream OBO API.
3. Start `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`.
4. Send `hi, run teams whoami` in Teams.
5. Complete the Bot Framework sign-in link and send the six-digit fallback code.
6. Retry `hi, run teams whoami`.

### Expected

- First run requests consent.
- Six-digit fallback completes delegated auth.
- Retried tool returns the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

### Actual

- First run returned `missing_consent`.
- Teams received the Bot Framework sign-in link.
- Six-digit fallback completed with `Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.`
- Retried `msteams_whoami` returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Teams missing-consent flow, Bot Framework sign-in link fallback, six-digit code completion, retrying `msteams_whoami`, and downstream OBO profile lookup.
- Edge cases checked: Six-digit messages are handled only while a pending sign-in challenge exists; delegated auth is rejected when missing/unconfigured/unavailable; Teams user-id fallback paths are covered by tests.
- What you did **not** verify: Non-Teams channels, production tenant rollout, hosted downstream API deployment, and every Teams client native OAuth-card rendering variant.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`Yes`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: Existing configs continue to work. To use delegated auth, explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess` and the Teams Bot Framework OAuth connection described in the docs.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A plugin could receive a user token unexpectedly.
  - Mitigation: Delegated auth is opt-in, allowlist-gated, and claim-validated before tool execution.
- Risk: Teams clients may render OAuth consent as a sign-in link instead of a native card.
  - Mitigation: The Teams implementation supports sign-in-link fallback and six-digit completion.
- Risk: Downstream API consent is separate from Teams bot consent.
  - Mitigation: Docs and examples use separate app registrations and document admin pre-consent for the downstream API.

## Rationale And Design Decisions

### Keep core generic

Delegated auth is modeled as a generic plugin capability instead of a Teams-specific special case in core. Core owns policy parsing, tool gating, token claim validation, and runtime propagation; the Teams plugin owns Bot Framework SSO behavior and token acquisition.

### Make delegated auth explicit and policy-gated

Plugin delegated auth is opt-in through `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess.enabled`, with optional provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type restrictions.

### Keep optional tools least-privilege

Optional plugin factories receive `ctx.auth` only when the plugin itself, `group:plugins`, `*`, or a concrete optional tool name is allowlisted. The resolver also handles implicit optional registrations where `names: []` and `declaredNames` carry the actual tool contract.

### Resolve auth per execution for cached descriptors

Cached plugin tool descriptors keep descriptor creation fast, but delegated auth is resolved when the cached tool executes, so a previous message’s auth context is never cached into a future run.

### Propagate auth through run plumbing, not prompts

The Teams delegated auth context is passed through hidden runtime/run parameters and plugin tool context, including queued replies, follow-up runs, embedded runner attempts, OpenClaw tools, and Codex app-server tool calls.

### Teams owns Bot Framework SSO details

The Teams plugin owns Bot Framework token exchange, verify-state, sign-in resource creation, sign-in-link fallback, six-digit code fallback, and Teams user-id fallback handling.

### Keep Graph access server-side in the example

The example plugin calls a local downstream API. The downstream API performs Microsoft Graph OBO using its own app registration and delegated permission grant, which keeps Graph client secrets and broader Graph behavior behind a production-shaped API boundary.

## Verification

- `pnpm tsgo:core --pretty false`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src --pretty false`
- `pnpm test src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.delegated-auth.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.delegated-auth-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions --pretty false`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test --pretty false`
- `pnpm test src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm dup:check:coverage`
- Final review pass: no actionable correctness/security/regression findings in the reviewed diff
- Manual Teams dev setup: consent fallback completed and `msteams_whoami` returned the signed-in user profile

target.title: docs(agent-loop): document idle-timeout cost-runaway circuit breaker
target.body:
## What

Adds a bullet to the Timeouts section of `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` documenting the idle-timeout circuit breaker introduced in #76345.

## Why

The existing Timeouts section explains that individual model requests abort on idle timeout, but says nothing about what happens when idle timeouts repeat. The circuit breaker — which halts further retries after 5 consecutive idle timeouts without completed model progress — is currently undocumented. Users who hit the `[idle-timeout-circuit-breaker-tripped]` error in logs have no docs to explain what they're seeing or why it fired.

## Accuracy

All claims in the added bullet are sourced directly from `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/idle-timeout-breaker.ts` and the CHANGELOG entry for #76345:
- Cap of 5: `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_IDLE_TIMEOUTS_BEFORE_OUTPUT = 5`
- Reset condition: `completedModelProgress` (completed text or tool-call progress), not partial output tokens
- Scope: fires across auth-profile retries inside the same embedded run
- Incident numbers: from the original issue #76293 report

target.title: fix(memory-core): clean stale short-term temp files
target.body:
## Summary

- clean stale orphaned `short-term-recall.json.*.tmp` and `phase-signals.json.*.tmp` files during short-term promotion repair
- preserve fresh temp files and unrelated temp-looking files so active or manual files are not swept
- surface `removedTempFiles` through memory-core repair summaries, doctor output, and the plugin SDK facade

Fixes #77888.

## Root cause

`writeStore` and `writePhaseSignalStore` write a sibling temp file and then rename it into place. A process crash or failed rename after the write can leave the temp file in `memory/.dreams` indefinitely because repair only normalized the recall store and stale lock.

target.title: fix(ui): add document MIME mappings (xlsx/docx/pptx/etc) for chat attachments — Bug #9
target.body:
## Summary

Sandpaw Bug #9 — Todd Bolyard's `go-yard` instance produced an Excel pricing analysis with his AI assistant ("Muffin"), but the browser only offered "Webpage Complete" as the Save As format for the `.xlsx`. The file was served with the wrong `Content-Type`, so the browser treated the response as an HTML page.

## Root cause

`ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.ts` infers an attachment's MIME type from a hand-maintained `MIME_BY_EXT` table when MEDIA references come back as plain URLs/paths. That table covered images, audio, video, `pdf`, `txt`, `md`, `csv`, `json`, and `zip` — but **none** of the common Office, OpenDocument, or source-code extensions. For an `.xlsx` upload the lookup returned `undefined`, `mediaKindFromMime(undefined)` returned `undefined` → fell through to `"document"` with no `mimeType`, and the downstream chat serving path emitted the file with a generic/HTML Content-Type. Hence Todd's "Webpage Complete" symptom.

## Fix

Extend `MIME_BY_EXT` to cover the full document set called out in the bug:

| Extension | MIME |
|---|---|
| `xlsx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` |
| `xls` | `application/vnd.ms-excel` |
| `docx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` |
| `doc` | `application/msword` |
| `pptx` | `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` |
| `ppt` | `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint` |
| `odt` / `ods` / `odp` | OpenDocument text/spreadsheet/presentation |
| `rtf` | `application/rtf` |
| `html` / `htm` | `text/html` |
| `xml` | `application/xml` |
| `yaml` / `yml` | `application/yaml` |
| `ts` / `js` / `py` / `sh` / `sql` | source-code text MIMEs |

`mediaKindFromMime` (in `src/media/constants.ts`) already classifies anything starting with `application/` or `text/` as `"document"`, so every new entry flows through without further changes — verified by reading the file before editing.

## Tests

Parameterized coverage added to `ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`:

- Each new Office Open XML, legacy Office, OpenDocument, PDF, and RTF extension produces an attachment with `kind: "document"` and the canonical MIME.
- `xlsx`, `docx`, `pptx`, and `pdf` (the cases called out in Bug #9) are explicitly asserted.
- `html` and `ts` cover the `text/*` and source-code paths.

```
✓ unit-ui ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts (39 tests) 10ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  39 passed (39)
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` are clean on the touched files.

## What this does NOT fix yet

Even with the correct MIME inferred, the gateway's outgoing-attachment pipeline is image-only (`src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts`). Documents still need a managed `/api/chat/media/outgoing/...` URL with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<original>"` to make Save As behave fully. That is **PR B** — `feat/managed-document-attachments-bug-9` — which I'm opening next.

This PR is the small, safe slice that immediately stops Office documents from being misclassified at the chat layer; it should ship today for Todd.

## Bug

Sandpaw Bug #9 — `go-yard` instance, file delivery for non-image documents.

## Review

🚫 Do not merge yet. Tagging Ada/Brian for Codex review per Brian's protocol.



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: before this PR, `MIME_BY_EXT` in
`ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.ts` had no entry for `.xlsx`,
`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xls`, `.doc`, `.ppt`, `.odt`/`.ods`/`.odp`, `.rtf`,
`.html`/`.htm`, `.xml`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, or common source-code
extensions. Office documents fell through with `mimeType` undefined,
which let the chat surface emit them with a generic/HTML
`Content-Type` and produced Todd Bolyard's "Webpage Complete" symptom.
This PR adds the full document set to `MIME_BY_EXT`.

**Real environment tested**: macOS 25.3.0 (arm64), Node v22.22.0, branch
`fix/document-mime-mappings-bug-9` at commit `119b702b4e`. This PR
touches a UI/TypeScript file; the real-runtime proof is to drive the
actual production build pipeline (Vite production build with
minification + tree-shaking) and inspect the artifact end users'
browsers will load. No mocks, no vitest; the bytes below are the
deployed bundle.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```sh
$ cd ui
$ pnpm build
> openclaw-ui@0.0.0 build /Users/ada/work/openclaw/ui
> vite build
...

✓ built in 1.75s

$ for ext in xlsx docx pptx; do

  done

$ for mime in \

**Observed result after fix**: the new MIME mappings introduced in

target.title: fix: scope provider resolution caches to catalog runs
target.body:
## Summary

Scopes provider-resolution caches to a single provider-catalog/catalog-auth operation instead of relying on repeated uncached plugin/provider lookups.

This adds an explicit `ProviderResolutionScope` and threads it through the provider catalog/auth/discovery/runtime paths so repeated deterministic lookups within the same catalog run are collapsed, including negative results.

Cached within the operation scope:

- `resolveProviderPluginsForHooks`
- `resolveProviderRuntimePlugin`
- runtime provider discovery lookups
- provider owning-plugin lookup
- synthetic provider auth lookup

The scope is intentionally per-operation rather than global/TTL-based to avoid stale provider/auth/plugin state across config reloads or plugin changes.

## Why

CPU profiles from a real gateway showed provider-catalog/auth work dominating startup/runtime profiles. The expensive path was not a single provider repeated under a shallow auth helper; many provider refs flowed through the same expensive plugin/runtime/synthetic-auth resolution path.

The earlier shallow auth memoization approach was removed because it did not produce measurable improvement on the real profile.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #75564
- Related #77649
- Related #62364
- Related #74058
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Repro + Verification

### Tests

node scripts/test-projects.mjs   src/agents/models-config.providers.implicit.discovery-scope.test.ts   src/agents/models-config.providers.auth-provenance.test.ts   src/plugins/provider-catalog.test.ts   src/plugins/capability-provider-runtime.test.ts   src/plugins/compaction-provider.test.ts   src/plugins/memory-embedding-provider-runtime.test.ts

70 tests passed
```

```text

exit 0
```

```text

clean
```

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Provider catalog/auth resolution spent excessive CPU repeatedly resolving provider plugin/runtime/discovery/synthetic-auth metadata inside one catalog operation. In the baseline 120s profile, `runProviderCatalogWithTimeout` accounted for ~26.44s inclusive, with `resolveCatalogProviderApiKey`, `resolveConfigBackedProviderAuth`, and `resolveProviderSyntheticAuthWithPlugin` among the main inclusive costs.

**Real environment tested:** Linux 6.14.0-33-generic x64, Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw `v2026.5.4` installed runtime under `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist`, patched with the V2 operation-scope-cache hotpatch. The patch markers were present in 5 installed dist files via `OPENCLAW_PATCH provider-resolution-scope-cache`.

**Exact steps or command run after fix:**
1. Applied `/data/fixes/patch-provider-resolution-scope-cache.sh` to the installed OpenClaw dist.
2. Confirmed the installed patch markers in:
   - `models-config-BNy6yvyP.js`
   - `models-config.providers.secrets-BZe0MB4X.js`
   - `provider-runtime-D2wRmWvE.js`
   - `provider-discovery.runtime-LG7Dw41m.js`
   - `providers-CIOnj-lk.js`
3. Captured a 120.1s patched profile from the live gateway: `/tmp/openclaw_running.cpuprofile`.
4. Compared it with the pre-V2/shallow-patch 120.1s profile: `/tmp/openclaw.cpuprofile`.
5. Captured an additional warm profile: `/tmp/openclaw_warmed.cpuprofile`.

**After-fix evidence:** Copied live profile output from the patched gateway:

```text
$ grep -R "OPENCLAW_PATCH provider-resolution-scope-cache" -n   /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/models-config-BNy6yvyP.js   /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/models-config.providers.secrets-BZe0MB4X.js   /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/provider-runtime-D2wRmWvE.js   /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/provider-discovery.runtime-LG7Dw41m.js   /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/providers-CIOnj-lk.js | wc -l
5
```

Before V2 operation-scope cache (`/tmp/openclaw.cpuprofile`, 120.1s):

```text
Profile /tmp/openclaw.cpuprofile: wall 120.1s, nodes=203298, samples=111299
26439.4ms  22.0%  runProviderCatalogWithTimeout
13224.9ms  11.0%  resolveCatalogProviderApiKey
11267.3ms   9.4%  resolveConfigBackedProviderAuth
11215.1ms   9.3%  resolveProviderSyntheticAuthWithPlugin
```

After V2 operation-scope cache (`/tmp/openclaw_running.cpuprofile`, 120.1s):

```text
Profile /tmp/openclaw_running.cpuprofile: wall 120.1s, nodes=172863, samples=111422
17269.2ms  14.4%  runProviderCatalogWithTimeout
 9210.7ms   7.7%  resolveCatalogProviderApiKey
 7186.5ms   6.0%  resolveConfigBackedProviderAuth
 7132.6ms   5.9%  resolveProviderSyntheticAuthWithPlugin
```

Warm follow-up profile (`/tmp/openclaw_warmed.cpuprofile`, 120.5s) no longer showed the catalog/auth functions above in the sampled hot set, but did expose a remaining adjacent plugin-registry/runtime-resolution hotspot:

```text
Total functions: 2761
Showing top 50, minMs=1

 TOTAL SELF FUNCTION
 17.124s 5.3ms loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadata
 16.784s 1.1ms resolveProviderPluginsForHooks
 15.305s 7.5ms loadInstalledPluginIndex
 15.295s 9.5ms buildInstalledPluginIndex
 14.500s 6.5ms resolveRuntimeProviderPluginLoadState
```

**Observed result after fix:** On the live patched gateway, the V2 operation-scope cache reduced the profiled catalog/auth costs by roughly 30-36%:

- `runProviderCatalogWithTimeout`: 26.44s -> 17.27s (~35% less)
- `resolveCatalogProviderApiKey`: 13.22s -> 9.21s (~30% less)
- `resolveConfigBackedProviderAuth`: 11.27s -> 7.19s (~36% less)
- `resolveProviderSyntheticAuthWithPlugin`: 11.22s -> 7.13s (~36% less)

**What was not tested:** A long multi-operator production soak was not run. The warm profile also shows remaining plugin-registry/installed-plugin-index/runtime-resolution CPU that this PR does not fully eliminate; that should be handled as a follow-up rather than claimed as solved here.

## Notes for reviewers

This PR is deliberately conservative: the cache lifetime is scoped to one catalog operation, so it should avoid stale global state. It is not intended to solve all provider/plugin runtime CPU usage; it specifically reduces repeated work within catalog/auth resolution.

target.title: [codex] Fix explicit custom web_search provider routing
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes `web_search` routing when `tools.web.search.provider` explicitly names a custom or installed web-search provider.

The agent tool wrapper was resolving late-bound runtime metadata and then allowing that runtime-selected provider to determine whether provider discovery should use the runtime registry or the bundled-only path. If the runtime metadata was stale, auto-detected, or computed before a custom provider was available in the active registry, an explicit config value could be ignored. That made an intentionally selected custom provider behave as if it were unknown or fall through to an unrelated bundled provider.

This PR makes the configured provider string the authoritative selection when it is present, and passes it through as `providerId` to the web-search runtime. The shared web-tool runtime context now also evaluates explicit config before runtime metadata when deciding whether to prefer runtime providers.

## Why This Is Needed

`tools.web.search.provider` is a user-facing explicit routing setting. When it is set, users reasonably expect that provider to be used, regardless of any prior runtime auto-detection metadata. The previous behavior inverted that precedence in the agent execution path:

- startup or secret-resolution metadata could record one provider as selected;
- the agent tool would trust that metadata first;
- provider candidate loading could then be scoped in a way that excluded the explicitly configured custom provider;
- `runWebSearch` would either throw an unknown-provider error for the configured provider or execute a different provider from the bundled set.

That is both surprising and risky. A configured provider can differ from an auto-detected provider in credentials, cost profile, data source, compliance properties, network path, or availability. Explicit config is intentionally a hard routing instruction, not a hint that stale metadata can override.

## What Changed

- `createWebSearchTool` now reads the configured `tools.web.search.provider` from the late-bound config snapshot and passes it to `runWebSearch` as `providerId`.
- `resolveWebToolRuntimeContext` now gives configured provider IDs precedence over runtime-selected metadata when deciding provider discovery mode.
- `resolveWebSearchCandidates` now reloads plugin web-search providers if an explicit provider ID was requested, runtime-provider discovery was preferred, and the active runtime registry did not contain that explicit provider.
- `docs/tools/web.md` now documents the compatibility choice: an explicit configured provider is a hard route and `web_search` fails instead of silently auto-detecting another provider if that provider cannot be loaded at runtime.

The fallback reload is intentionally narrow: it only runs for explicit provider requests that are missing from the first candidate set. Normal bundled-provider and auto-detect paths keep their existing behavior.

## Impact

Users with a configured bundled provider should see no behavior change other than stronger explicit-provider precedence. Users with installed/custom web-search providers get deterministic routing when they set `tools.web.search.provider`.

The failure mode also becomes clearer: if the explicit provider still cannot be discovered after the fallback load, the runtime reports the configured provider as unknown instead of silently drifting to another provider.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent `web_search` should honor an explicit `tools.web.search.provider` selection even when runtime web-search metadata is stale and points at a different provider. The intended compatibility choice is fail-closed explicit provider routing, not silent fallback to auto-detect.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw repo runtime on Linux in this isolated PR worktree, using production TypeScript modules via `pnpm exec tsx`; no gateway restart, no host config writes, and no real credentials.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a production-module terminal proof that installed a synthetic active plugin registry with `stale` and `custom` web-search providers, configured `tools.web.search.provider: "custom"`, supplied stale runtime metadata selecting `stale`, and executed the agent `web_search` tool with query `routing proof`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the production-module proof:

```text
pnpm exec tsx -e '<production-module routing proof>'
agent_tool_explicit_custom_over_stale_runtime {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\n  \"query\": \"routing proof\",\n  \"provider\": \"custom\"\n}"}],"details":{"query":"routing proof","provider":"custom"}}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The agent tool returned provider `custom`, proving the explicit configured provider won over stale runtime metadata selecting `stale`.
- **What was not tested:** No live third-party search API call was made because the bug is provider routing before network execution; focused regression tests cover the runtime discovery and unknown-provider fail-closed paths.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md docs/tools/web.md src/agents/tools/web-search.ts src/agents/tools/web-tool-runtime-context.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.enabled-defaults.test.ts src/web-search/runtime.ts src/web-search/runtime.test.ts`
- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/web-search.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.enabled-defaults.test.ts src/web-search/runtime.test.ts`
- `pnpm changed:lanes --json` selected `core`, `coreTests`, and `docs`.
- `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled pnpm check:changed` was attempted because Testbox is not authenticated here; it completed conflict-marker, changelog attribution, dependency/patch guards, core typecheck, core test typecheck, core lint, runtime sidecar loader, and runtime import-cycle checks, then left an idle node process with no active child work and was stopped to avoid leaving it behind.
- `pnpm check:docs`

Testbox was attempted first but is unavailable in this environment:

```text
blacksmith testbox warmup ci-check-testbox.yml --ref main --idle-timeout 90
blacksmith testbox list
# Error: not authenticated — run 'blacksmith auth login' first
```

Known unrelated broad-check note: `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` currently reports `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` hash drift even though this branch has no generated file changes and does not touch Plugin SDK exports.

target.title: fix(agents): classify already-at-target edit follower as noop (#60816)
target.body:
### Summary

Reported by @bboguri in #60816: when two identical edits run concurrently against the same file, the leader mutates the file successfully but the follower's `base.execute(...)` then throws `Could not find the exact text in <path>` because the leader already replaced `oldText`. The wrapped recovery layer in `src/agents/pi-tools.host-edit.ts:wrapEditToolWithRecovery` had two recovery branches (convert post-write throws to success when the file changed, and append the current file contents to mismatch errors) but no third branch for "the file is unchanged AND already at the requested target state". The follower therefore surfaced as either a misleading error (rethrown mismatch) or, on certain edge inputs, a false success.

clawsweeper-bot's review on this issue prescribed the exact fix shape:

> Add a focused post-state classifier around edit mismatch handling, returning normal success only for writes this request performed, a distinct non-error noop when the requested final state is already satisfied, and preserving errors for true mismatches or write failures.

This PR adds that third branch, gated on the exact-text mismatch error class so unrelated thrown errors keep rethrowing untouched (addresses the [P2] clawsweeper review note on the previous push).

### Fix

`src/agents/pi-tools.host-edit.ts`:

1. New helper `isFileAlreadyInTargetState({ originalContent, currentContent, edits })` returns true only when the originalContent snapshot equals the current file contents AND every edit's newText is present in the file AND every edit's oldText is absent from the file.
2. New helper `buildEditNoopResult(pathParam)` returns the prescribed copy `Edit noop: content already up to date in <path>.` distinct from the existing `Successfully replaced text in <path>.` used by the post-write recovery branch.
3. `wrapEditToolWithRecovery` consults the noop classifier inside the existing `shouldAddMismatchHint(err)` block, after `didEditLikelyApply` (so genuine post-write throws still report success) and before `appendMismatchHint` (so a false-positive mismatch on a follower no longer re-throws). Any error outside the exact-text mismatch class (aborts, access failures, sandbox bridge errors) keeps rethrowing unchanged.

True mismatches (oldText still present) and write failures (file actually different from the requested state) continue to throw the existing `appendMismatchHint`-decorated error unchanged.

### Tests

`src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-edit-recovery.test.ts`:

- Pin the canonical follower scenario for #60816 (file already in target state, mocked execute throws the exact mismatch, recovery returns the noop result).
- Same contract under the multi-edit `edits[]` shape (two edits, both targets satisfied, both oldText absent).
- Negative pin: true mismatch where newText is present but oldText is also still present (the noop classifier must NOT fire and the mismatch error must rethrow with current file contents).
- New regression for the [P2] clawsweeper review: unrelated thrown error (sandbox bridge timeout) on a file that is already at the target state must rethrow the original error untouched.

### Changelog

Added one bullet under `## Unreleased` -> `### Fixes` in `CHANGELOG.md`, citing #60816 and `Thanks @jeffrey701` per repo convention, noting the gating on the exact-text mismatch error class.

### Note on unrelated CI red

`check-test-types` and `check` are red on this PR head, but every failure is in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-tts.test.ts` (lines 125-198, `'reply' is possibly 'undefined'` and similar). That file was last touched by upstream commit `048a50cfe1 test: tighten auto reply timestamps` on `main` two hours before this push and is not modified by this PR.

Fixes #60816.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Concurrent identical edits on the same file (leader has already replaced `oldText` -> `newText` before the follower's `base.execute(...)` runs). Pre-fix the follower surfaces as either a rethrown `Could not find the exact text in <path>` mismatch or, on edge inputs, a false `Successfully replaced` claim. After this patch the follower is classified as `Edit noop: content already up to date in <path>.`, and only on the exact-text mismatch error class - sandbox bridge / abort / access errors keep rethrowing untouched.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-23-generic, Node.js v22.22.0, Bash terminal, this PR head `c3b613fdba` checked out. The reproducer below imports `wrapEditToolWithRecovery` directly from `src/agents/pi-tools.host-edit.ts` (no mocks of the wrapper itself) and drives it against real files in a real `mkdtemp` directory.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the reproducer below from a fresh shell after checkout of `c3b613fdba`. Command:

    cd /path/to/openclaw
    node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/77638-repro.mts

Reproducer source (`/tmp/77638-repro.mts`), same shape as the four scenarios pinned in the test file, run end-to-end against the wrapper and real `fs`:

    import fs from "node:fs/promises";
    import os from "node:os";
    import path from "node:path";
    import { wrapEditToolWithRecovery } from ".../src/agents/pi-tools.host-edit.ts";

    const tmpDir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "openclaw-77638-repro-"));

    function makeTool(opts) {
      const base = { name: "edit", execute: async () => opts.exec() };
      return wrapEditToolWithRecovery(base, {
        root: tmpDir,
        readFile: (p) => fs.readFile(p, "utf-8"),
      });
    }

    // Scenario A: follower already at target - leader replaced "old text" -> "new text"
    // Scenario B: non-mismatch error (sandbox bridge timeout) at target state
    // Scenario C: true mismatch (oldText still present alongside newText)
    // Scenario D: post-write throw with real file change

Evidence after fix: terminal capture from `node` running the reproducer above, stdout copied live and indented (no leading hash, so it cannot be confused with a markdown heading):

    tmpDir = /tmp/openclaw-77638-repro-NDiz8q

    Scenario A: follower already at target -> Edit noop
      isError=false
      text="Edit noop: content already up to date in /tmp/openclaw-77638-repro-NDiz8q/demo1.txt."
      -> OK

    Scenario B: non-mismatch error at target -> rethrows untouched
      -> THREW: Sandbox bridge timed out before edit could run

    Scenario C: true mismatch (oldText still present) -> hint rethrow
      -> THREW: Could not find the exact text in demo3.txt. The old text must match exactly including all whitespace and newlines.
    Current file contents:
    old text and new text both here

    Scenario D: post-write throw with real file change -> Successfully replaced
      isError=false
      text="Successfully replaced text in /tmp/openclaw-77638-repro-NDiz8q/demo4.txt."
      -> OK

    repro complete

Observed result after fix: Scenario A (canonical #60816 follower) returned `isError: false` with content text `Edit noop: content already up to date in /tmp/openclaw-77638-repro-NDiz8q/demo1.txt.` so the new third branch fired and the misleading mismatch and the false `Successfully replaced` are both gone. Scenario B (the [P2] regression) rethrew `Sandbox bridge timed out before edit could run` verbatim because the noop classifier did NOT fire (underlying error was not the exact-text mismatch class) even though the file was at the target state. Scenario C rethrew `Could not find the exact text in demo3.txt.` enriched with `Current file contents: old text and new text both here` so the existing `appendMismatchHint` recovery is preserved when oldText is still present. Scenario D returned `Successfully replaced text in /tmp/openclaw-77638-repro-NDiz8q/demo4.txt.` so the existing `didEditLikelyApply` recovery still fires.

What was not tested: I did not run the full live concurrent-edits race against a running OpenClaw agent talking to the pinned `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent@0.73.0` upstream over `withFileMutationQueue`; the reproducer drives the wrapper directly with throw-shapes that match what the upstream tool emits, mirroring the test fixtures.
